About.title: About QR Gate Access Control
About.subtitle: Access control platform for libraries and organizations
About.overview: This system combines gate QR issuance and validation, member and gate management, access history, and Thai national ID card reading via DUALi DE-620 smart card readers for fast member registration.
About.capQr: Issue and validate entry/exit QR codes with signed tokens and policy-based expiry
About.capGate: Manage gates, branches, devices, and officer gate dashboards
About.capMember: Member lifecycle, renewals, access history, and reporting
About.capIdCard: Thai ID card reading (web + reader hardware) for registration
About.capSecurity: RBAC, audit logs, rate limiting, and PDPA-oriented design
About.techNote: Monorepo: Next.js frontend + Python FastAPI backend for card reading
About.structureFrontend: frontend/ — Next.js app, Prisma, Mantine admin UI
About.developedBy: Development by KKU Library IT Team

IdCard.extensionEasyInstallHintWindows: Install it, then enable Bridge in the extension popup — no localhost in the URL.

IdCard.extensionEasyStep2: In Chrome: extension popup → Test Native Host → Enable Bridge
IdCard.extensionChromeUrlCopied: Copied — paste in Chrome address bar
IdCard.serverCardApiWarningBody: Server Card API cannot see the USB reader on this PC.
IdCard.extensionStep1: Download the .zip and extract to a permanent folder.
IdCard.extensionStep2: Open chrome://extensions → Developer mode → Load unpacked → select the extracted folder.
IdCard.extensionStep3: Copy the extension ID from chrome://extensions.
IdCard.extensionStep4: Install the native host (command below) and restart Chrome.
IdCard.extensionStep5: Open the extension popup → Test native host → Enable Bridge → refresh the ID card page.
IdCard.extensionPythonNote: Install Python 3.12 and backend/requirements.txt on this PC first (see extension/README.md).
IdCard.scanDesc: Use your phone camera to scan the QR Code below to receive your E-Ticket.
IdCard.de620WindowsDriverTitle: Card API is up but DE-620 not found — install a Windows driver
IdCard.de620WindowsDriverBody: If /api/readers returns {"readers":[]} with USB plugged in, Windows lacks a driver Card API can use.
IdCard.de620WindowsDriverOptionDuali: Install DUALi DE-620 driver (InstallDriver64bit_Sign.msi from SDK/CD), then restart KKU Card API
IdCard.de620WindowsDriverOptionZadig: Or use Zadig to install WinUSB for DUALi DE-620 (Options → List All Devices → Replace Driver with WinUSB)
IdCard.de620WindowsDriverAfter: After driver install: Quit KKU Card API from tray → restart → click Refresh or open http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/diagnostic
IdCard.errorConnect: DUALi DE-620 not found. Insert a card and ensure the Python server is running.
IdCard.errorBackend: Cannot reach the card reader backend (port 8000). Start the Python server.
IdCard.errorInsertCard: No card in reader. Please insert the card firmly.
IdCard.errorRead: Could not read from card. Please insert it firmly.
IdCard.errorExpired: ⚠️ Warning: This ID card has expired.
IdCard.errorGeneral: An error occurred during card reading.
IdCard.winUsbSubtitle: Required for Windows to use DE-620
IdCard.winUsbWhyBody: DUALi DE-620 uses Vendor Protocol for communication, which Windows does not have a built-in driver for. You must install the WinUSB driver via Zadig before using the reader.
IdCard.winUsbStep2Desc: Plug in the reader → Options → List All Devices → select "DUALi DE-620"
IdCard.winUsbStep3Title: Select WinUSB and click Install Driver
IdCard.winUsbStep3Desc: Ensure Driver is "WinUSB" and click "Install Driver" or "Replace Driver"
